title: Warranty Vault
pitch: Warranty Vault is a personal warranty management web app for tracking products, purchase details, warranty coverage, invoices, manuals, warranty cards, and other supporting documents in one place.
about_excerpt: Warranty Vault is a personal warranty management web app for tracking products, purchase details, warranty coverage, invoices, manuals, warranty cards, and other supporting documents in one place. Like Comment Story Updates Home Page for Warranty Vault after user login Add warranty page Chart of remaining warranty per product List of WebMCP tools, from Chrome Agent using tool to create a new warranty item Agent conversing in Hindi+English to user for fethcing details of warranty Preview of uploaded warranty doc through Codex Agent Warranty Vault Inspiration Whenever we buy a product—an AC, TV, laptop, mobile phone, or home appliance—we receive product and warranty information in different ways. Sometimes we have to register the warranty manually on a website. Sometimes the information is available in a Gmail purchase email, invoice, PDF, receipt, or warranty document . The information already exists digitally, but we still have to manually organize it. To keep track of a warranty, users often have to search their emails, find the invoice or warranty document, read it, and manually copy details such as the product name, brand, model number, serial number, purchase date, price, warranty period, and expiry date into another application. Months or years later, when the warranty is about to expire—or when the product develops an issue—we have to search through the same old emails, PDFs, and invoices again. This made us ask a simple question: Why should users manually enter and search for information that already exists digitally? That question inspired us to build Warranty Vault . Warranty Vault brings the complete warranty lifecycle into one place—from capturing warranty information from Gmail to tracking expiry and helping users extend or claim their warranty when they need it. With WebMCP , Warranty Vault becomes agent-ready, allowing AI agents to understand the application's capabilities and perform structured actions on behalf of the user. What it does Warranty Vault is a smart warranty management application designed to eliminate repetitive manual warranty entry and simplify warranty management throughout the product lifecycle. Instead of manually finding an email, reading an invoice, and entering every field into Warranty Vault, a user can simply ask: "Find my AC warranty email in Gmail and add it to Warranty Vault." The AI can find the relevant purchase or warranty email in Gmail, understand the information, extract the required product and warranty details, and use Warranty Vault's WebMCP capabilities to create the warranty record. Warranty Vault can maintain information such as: Product name Brand Product category Model number Serial number Purchase date Purchase price Retailer or seller Warranty duration Warranty start date Warranty expiry date Invoice and supporting information But Warranty Vault doesn't stop after saving the warranty. It continues to help users throughout the complete warranty lifecycle . Warranty Expiry Tracking Warranty Vault keeps track of warranty expiry dates so users don't have to remember them manually. When a product is approaching its warranty expiry date, Warranty Vault can surface that information to the user so they can take action before it is too late. Claim Warranty If a product develops an issue while it is still under warranty, the user can initiate a warranty claim directly from the product record . Instead of searching again for the invoice, purchase date, model number, or warranty information, Warranty Vault already has the required product context available. Our complete experience is: Gmail / Invoice / PDF → AI extracts details → WebMCP → Warranty Vault → Track Expiry How we built it We started by building Warranty Vault as a structured product and warranty management web application . Users can manually add and manage warranties, but we didn't want to build another application where users simply move information from one form to another. The biggest opportunity was eliminating that repetitive manual entry. That's where WebMCP became an important part of the solution. We used WebMCP to make Warranty Vault agent-ready by exposing meaningful, structured capabilities that an AI agent can understand and use. Instead of requiring an AI agent to visually navigate the website, locate every input field, enter information, and click buttons, WebMCP allows Warranty Vault to expose the actions available to an agent and the information required to perform them. For our Gmail use case, the journey works like this: The user gives a natural-language instruction: "Find my AC warranty email in Gmail and add it to Warranty Vault." The AI searches Gmail for the relevant purchase or warranty email. It reads the relevant email and identifies the product and warranty information. It extracts available information such as product name, brand, model number, purchase date, purchase price, and warranty period. The extracted information is converted into the structured fields required by Warranty Vault. The AI discovers the relevant capability exposed by Warranty Vault through WebMCP. The agent provides the structured warranty information to Warranty Vault. Warranty Vault validates the information and creates the warranty record. This transforms the traditional experience from: Search Gmail → Open Email → Open Invoice → Read → Copy Details → Open Warranty App → Fill Form → Save into: Ask → AI understands → WebMCP acts → Warranty saved We also designed the experience around higher-level user actions rather than individual UI interactions. For example: Add Warranty Extend Warranty Claim Warranty This allows WebMCP to support the warranty lifecycle rather than simply automate form filling. Challenges we ran into One of the biggest challenges was that warranty information is not standardized . Different manufacturers and retailers provide product and warranty information differently. One Gmail message might contain all the required information directly in the email. Another might contain only basic purchase information with an attached invoice or PDF. Some documents clearly specify the warranty duration, while others may not mention it at all. This created an important challenge: How do we allow AI to understand unstructured information while keeping the data stored in Warranty Vault structured and reliable? We also had to think carefully about missing information. For example, if a purchase email doesn't contain a serial number or clearly specify the warranty duration, the AI should not invent information simply to complete the record. Another challenge was deciding what capabilities should be exposed through WebMCP. Instead of thinking about low-level interactions such as: "Click this button." or "Fill this field." we focused on meaningful user goals: "Add this warranty." "Extend this warranty."
